summary: Early-1950s steel MC-39 fire tower at Montgomery Bell State Park, Dickson County; unstaffed since the mid-1970s; NHLR-registered 2023.

facts.design: Steel International Derrick MC-39 tower, about 80 feet tall, with steel stair treads and wood landings
facts.status_note: A Tennessee Landforms list marks the tower as removed, but a February 2023 visit describes it as overall in decent shape.

access.note: On the grounds of the Highland Rim district headquarters inside Montgomery Bell State Park. Normally open on weekdays during business hours and closed on weekends, per the register; closed for storm cleanup at a February 2023 visit.

events.note: The register says only early 1950s; 1950 is the start of that range
Last used for fire detection in the mid-1970s, per the district forester; no exact year given
Visit report dated February 13, 2023 describes condition, staffing and access

notes_for_editor: The register gives only early 1950s for the build date, so the 1950 event year is the start of that range, not a sourced year. The register misspells the county once as Dickinson; its own location line says Dickson, which matches the record. Status conflict: Tennessee Landforms lists the tower as removed (GC2560 6-15 removed), while the register's February 2023 visit found it standing. Left unresolved; status stays standing with a status_note. The register's 5,000-acre park figure is not used because other sources give a smaller park. The access and visit facts come from one 2023 visit report and may be out of date; no source is newer. The register's sign note says climbing is at the user's risk, but the forester advised against it, so climbable is recorded as false. The register's photo is credited to Jerry Lutes with no image URL captured, so no photo was added. Not verified: whether the tower still stands after 2023, and any fire it watched.
